chunks.text:
Famotidine is a histamine-2 blocker that works by decreasing the amount of acid the stomach produces.
Famotidine is used to treat and prevent ulcers in the stomach and intestines.
Famotidine also treats conditions in which the stomach produces too much acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
Famotidine treats gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
Famotidine treats other conditions in which acid backs up from the stomach into the esophagus.
This acid backup causes heartburn.
The Zantac 360 brand of Famotidine does not contain ranitidine.
Ranitidine is a medicine.
Ranitidine was withdrawn from market in the United States.

chunks.text:
Before taking famotidine, tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease.
Tell your doctor if you have a history of Long QT syndrome.
Tell your doctor if you have stomach cancer or other problems.
Tell your doctor if you have asthma, COPD, or other breathing problems.
Famotidine may be only part of a complete program of treatment that also includes changes in diet or lifestyle habits.
Follow your doctor's instructions very closely.
Heartburn is often confused with the first symptoms of a heart attack.
Seek emergency medical attention if you have chest pain or heavy feeling, pain spreading to the jaw, arm or shoulder, nausea, sweating, anxiety, light-headedness and a general ill feeling.
Do not use over-the-counter famotidine without a doctor's advice if you have trouble or pain swallowing food.
Do not use over-the-counter famotidine without a doctor's advice if you are vomiting with blood.
Do not use over-the-counter famotidine without a doctor's advice if you have bloody or black stools.
These may be signs of a serious condition.

chunks.text:
You should not use Famotidine if you are allergic to famotidine.
You should not use Famotidine if you are allergic to similar medicines.
Similar medicines include ranitidine (Zantac), cimetidine (Tagamet), or nizatidine (Axid).
To make sure Famotidine is safe for you, tell your doctor or pharmacist if you have ever had:
kidney disease;
liver disease;
cancer stomach; or
long QT syndrome (in you or a family member).
Ask a doctor before using famotidine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
Famotidine injection may contain an ingredient that can cause serious side effects or death in very young or premature babies.
Do not give Famotidine injection to a newborn or premature baby.

chunks.text:
Use famotidine exactly as directed on the label, or as prescribed by your doctor.
Famotidine oral is taken by mouth.
Famotidine injection is given as an infusion into a vein.
A healthcare provider will give you Famotidine if you are unable to take the medicine by mouth.
You may take famotidine oral with or without food.
Shake the bottle of Pepcid suspension (liquid) vigorously for 5 to 10 seconds prior to each use.
Measure the liquid medicine carefully.
Use the dosing syringe provided, or use a medicine dose-measuring device (not a kitchen spoon).
Most ulcers heal within 4 weeks of treatment.
Ulcers may take up to 8 weeks of using this medicine before your ulcer heals.
Keep using the medication as directed.
Call your doctor if the condition you are treating with this medicine does not improve, or if condition gets worse while using this medicine.
Famotidine may be only part of a complete program of treatment that also includes changes in diet or lifestyle habits.
Follow all instructions of your doctor or dietitian.
Store at room temperature away from moisture, heat, and light.

Drinking alcohol can increase the risk of damage to your stomach.
Avoid taking other stomach acid reducers unless your doctor has told you to.
However, you may take an antacid with famotidine.
Examples of antacids include Maalox, Mylanta, Gaviscon, Milk of Magnesia, Rolaids, and Tums.

chunks.text:
Get emergency medical help if you have any signs of an allergic reaction to famotidine.
Signs of an allergic reaction to famotidine include hives.
Signs of an allergic reaction to famotidine also include difficult breathing.
Signs of an allergic reaction to famotidine also include swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Stop using Famotidine and call your doctor at once if you have:
confusion, hallucinations, agitation, lack of energy;
a seizure;
fast or pounding heartbeats, sudden dizziness (like you might pass out).
Some side effects may be more likely in older adults and in people who have severe kidney disease.
Common famotidine side effects may include:
headache;
dizziness; or
constipation or diarrhea.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

chunks.section_heading: What other drugs will interact with famotidine?
chunks.text:
Famotidine oral can make it harder for your body to absorb other medicines you take by mouth.
Tell your doctor if you are taking:
cefditoren;
dasatinib;
delavirdine;
fosamprenavir; or
tizanidine.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may interact with famotidine.
These include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.
